explanation: The article's §Background puts the Kenyan invasion on ground the Ethiopian war left: "During the Ethiopian invasion of Somalia aimed at toppling the Islamic Courts Union administration, Kenyan troops assisted the Ethiopians and allied Somali forces in capturing the retreating Somali Islamists. Al-Shabaab viewed the Kenyan government with hostility ever since." Its §Lead up and planning adds that "After Ethiopian troops withdrew from Somalia in early 2009, Al-Shabaab came to control much of the south." So the earlier war is what made Kenya a target of al-Shabaab and what left al-Shabaab holding the ground Kenya invaded. `precondition-of` and not `caused`: the article gives the immediate trigger as a series of kidnappings on Kenyan territory in October 2011, which this atlas holds no record of, and says the intervention plan "was discussed and decided in 2010". Probable: Wikipedia alone.
